newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France ships performing horses to New York.
newsitem.headline: Air France ships performing horses to New York.

text.p: Air France said it will be shipping 26 performing horses from Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport to New York-JFK on Thursday.
The horses,from the Paris-based Zingaro hippodrome, are to take part in a New York revue organised by the Brooklyn Academy of Music.
"The horses will be shipped out from CDG to New York aboard two of our scheduled flights - a Boeing 747-200F and a 747-200 combi," an Air France cargo official told Reuters.

The horses, with an average weight of 600 kilos, will be transported in 12 stalls and accompanied aboard the aircraft by Zingaro owner and choreographer, Bartabas, along with grooms and lads and veterinary staff, the official said.
The horses will perform in New York from September 17 to November 10 and will return to France aboard Air France aircraft, the official added.
Air France transported around 100 thoroughbred horses in 1995 mainly to major racing events in the U.S., Dubai and the Far East.
The French state airline has a stock of 35 aircraft horse stalls which can each contain one to three animals, the official said.
